notes: Statutory penalty ranges for privacy regimes. Amounts are taken from the cited primary text. Where a statute is inflation-adjusted the registry stores the published figures with the adjustment date; update this file when a new adjustment is published. per_violation regimes multiply the count of violations pleaded in the case by the per-violation amount; fixed_or_turnover regimes take the higher of the fixed amount and a percentage of the undertaking's total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year.

statutes.name: GDPR Art. 83(5) - higher-tier administrative fine
statutes.enforcer: Lead supervisory authority (or DPA of the main establishment)
statutes.scope: Basic principles for processing incl. consent (Arts. 5, 6, 7, 9); data subject rights (Arts. 12-22); transfers to third countries (Arts. 44-49); Member State law under Chapter IX; non-compliance with an Art. 58(2) order

aggregation.description: If an undertaking infringes several provisions of the Regulation in the same or linked processing operations, the total amount of the fine must not exceed the amount specified for the gravest infringement.

statutes.notes: Ceiling applies per infringement against an undertaking; Art. 83(2) factors decide where inside the ceiling the fine lands. Precedent ratios observed in this dataset are far below 1.0 - the ceiling is a legal maximum, not an expectation.

sources.quote: Infringements of the following provisions shall, in accordance with paragraph 2, be subject to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

statutes.name: GDPR Art. 83(4) - lower-tier administrative fine
statutes.scope: Obligations of controller and processor under Arts. 8, 11, 25-39, 42 and 43; certification bodies (Arts. 42, 43); monitoring body (Art. 41(4))

aggregation.description: Linked processing operations: total fine capped at the amount for the gravest infringement.

statutes.notes: Security of processing (Art. 32) and data protection by design (Art. 25) sit in this lower tier, which is why breach cases (British Airways, Marriott) are cited against Art. 83(5)/83(4) in different analyses - check which provision the decision itself cites.

sources.quote: Infringements of the following provisions shall, in accordance with paragraph 2, be subject to administrative fines up to 10 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 2 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

statutes.name: GDPR Art. 83(6) - non-compliance with a supervisory authority order
statutes.scope: Non-compliance with an order by the supervisory authority referred to in Art. 58(2)

aggregation.description: Linked processing operations: total fine capped at the amount for the gravest infringement.

statutes.notes: Distinct from the periodic penalty payments a supervisory authority may impose under Art. 83(6) read with Art. 58(3) - those are calculated per day and must be recorded with a 'days' value in the case spec.

sources.quote: Non-compliance with an order by the supervisory authority as referred to in Article 58(2) shall, in accordance with paragraph 2 of this Article, be subject to administrative fines up to 20 000 000 EUR, or in the case of an undertaking, up to 4 % of the total worldwide annual turnover of the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

statutes.name: UK GDPR / DPA 2018 - higher maximum amount
statutes.scope: Infringements of the UK GDPR where Art. 83 specifies an amount, and failures to comply with an information, assessment, interview or enforcement notice; specified Part 3 and Part 4 failures

aggregation.description: Linked processing operations: total fine capped at the amount for the gravest infringement.

statutes.notes: Ceiling is per infringement but the ICO's fining guidance applies a five-step calculation inside it, including a turnover-based starting point.

sources.quote: The 'higher maximum amount' is, in the case of an undertaking, £17,500,000 or 4% of the undertaking's total annual worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

statutes.name: UK GDPR / DPA 2018 - standard maximum amount
statutes.scope: UK GDPR infringements where Art. 83 does not specify an amount, and Part 3 / Part 4 failures not listed for the higher maximum
statutes.notes: Rarely used in practice for UK GDPR breaches because Art. 83 supplies amounts that are imported by s.157(1)(a).

sources.quote: The 'standard maximum amount' is, in the case of an undertaking, £8,700,000 or 2% of the undertaking's total annual worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

statutes.name: CCPA/CPRA - civil penalty in an action by the Attorney General
statutes.scope: Any violation of the CCPA/CPRA by a business, service provider, contractor or other person, after a 30-day cure period

aggregation.description: The statute sets no aggregate cap: exposure is per violation x count. Every published AG settlement has nevertheless been a lump sum far below the arithmetic ceiling.

statutes.inflation_note: The CPPA's inflation adjustment (Cal. Civ. Code s. 1798.199.95(d)) put the figures at $2,663 and $7,988 effective 1 January 2025. The adjusted figures come from a secondary source and should be confirmed against the CPPA's own text before use.
statutes.citation_notes: s.1798.155(a) is the CPPA's administrative fine (same amounts); s.1798.155(b) is the AG's civil penalty.

sources.quote: Any business, service provider, or other person that violates this title shall be subject to an injunction and liable for a civil penalty of not more than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation or seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500) for each intentional violation

statutes.name: CCPA/CPRA - administrative fine in an action by the CPPA
statutes.scope: Any violation of the CCPA/CPRA by a business, service provider, contractor or other person; violations involving consumers the business knows are under 16 are always at the higher rate

aggregation.description: No aggregate cap in the statute.

statutes.inflation_note: Same inflation adjustment as the AG penalty ($2,663 / $7,988 effective 1 January 2025, secondary source).

sources.quote: Any business, service provider, contractor, or other person that violates this title shall be liable for an administrative fine of not more than two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each violation or seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500) for each intentional violation or violations involving the personal information of consumers whom the business ... has actual knowledge are under 16 years of age

statutes.name: CCPA - private right of action for data breaches
statutes.scope: Unauthorised access and exfiltration, theft or disclosure of non-encrypted, non-redacted personal information resulting from failure to maintain reasonable security
statutes.notes: Statutory damages of $100-$750 per consumer per incident, or actual damages, whichever is greater; the statute states the range is 'as adjusted' so check for a current CPI-adjusted figure. Cure is not available for this claim.

sources.quote: To recover damages in an amount not less than one hundred dollars ($100) and not greater than seven hundred and fifty ($750) per consumer per incident or actual damages, whichever is greater.

statutes.name: COPPA Rule - civil penalty per violation
statutes.enforcer: Federal Trade Commission / Department of Justice
statutes.citation: 15 U.S.C. 45(l), (m)(1)(A)-(B); 16 CFR Part 1 Subpart L; 16 CFR Part 312
statutes.scope: Violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Rule (notice, verifiable parental consent, data retention and disclosure limits)

aggregation.description: No statutory aggregate cap; each violation of a rule or order is a separate penalty.

statutes.inflation_note: 2025 level of $53,088 continues to apply in 2026: the FTC announced no inflation adjustment for 2026 (Federal Register notice, 15 September 2026).

sources.quote: A court can hold operators who violate the Rule liable for civil penalties of up to $53,088 per violation.
Section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 45(m)(1)(A)-$53,088
the FTC's civil penalty amounts will remain unchanged during 2026. The FTC will continue to apply the 2025 civil penalty levels.

statutes.name: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule - civil penalty per violation per day
statutes.enforcer: Federal Trade Commission / Department of Justice
statutes.citation: 15 U.S.C. 45(m)(1)(A); 16 CFR Part 318 (Health Breach Notification Rule); 16 CFR 1.98
statutes.scope: Failure by a vendor of personal health records, or a related entity, to notify individuals, the FTC and the media of an unauthorised disclosure of individually identifiable health information
statutes.notes: The FTC treats a failure to notify as a continuing violation, so days matter as much as the number of affected individuals; supply a 'days' value in the case spec.

sources.quote: GoodRx will be prohibited from sharing user health data with applicable third parties for advertising purposes, and has agreed to pay a $1.5 million civil penalty for violating the rule.
Section 5(m)(1)(A) of the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 45(m)(1)(A)-$53,088

statutes.name: HIPAA - civil money penalty tiers
statutes.scope: Violations of the HIPAA Administrative Simplification provisions (Privacy, Security, Breach Notification Rules)

tiers.when: did not know and, with reasonable diligence, would not have known of the violation
reasonable cause and not willful neglect
willful neglect, not corrected within 30 days

aggregation.description: For violations occurring on or after 18 February 2009, the penalty may not exceed the annual cap for identical violations during a calendar year; the cap is the tier-4 maximum.

statutes.inflation_note: Per-violation amounts are inflation-adjusted annually under the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act; the figures here are the latest published pair for each tier in 45 CFR 102.3 (tier maxima 73,011 / annual cap 2,190,294). Re-read 45 CFR 102.3 before relying on them.

sources.quote: In excess of $1,500,000 for identical violations during a calendar year ... In the amount of more than $100 for each violation
45 CFR 160.404(b)(2)(iv)(A),(B) OCR ... Maximum 73,011 ... Calendar Year Cap 2,190,294
sources.quality: regulation text (45 CFR 102.3 annual adjustment table)

statutes.name: Texas CUBI - capture or use of biometric identifier
statutes.scope: Capturing a biometric identifier for a commercial purpose, and related retention/disclosure limits, without the required notice and consent

aggregation.description: Civil penalty of not more than $25,000 for each violation; the AG's office has treated unauthorised capture and improper storage as separate violations, which can double exposure per individual.

statutes.notes: No private right of action; the AG alone enforces. The per-violation ceiling across a large population is effectively unbounded - the Texas meta-settlement was far below it.

sources.quote: (d) A person who violates this section is subject to a civil penalty of not more than $25,000 for each violation. The attorney general may bring an action to recover the civil penalty.

statutes.name: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act - civil penalty
statutes.scope: Violations of TDPSA duties: notice, consent for sensitive data, consumer rights requests, data security, sensitive-data assessment

aggregation.description: Up to $7,500 per violation; a 30-day cure period applies before the AG may act.

statutes.notes: Section number for the penalty provision should be pinned to the current codification before filing; the statute has been amended since enactment.

sources.quote: The State claims entitlement to more than $1,000,000 in monetary relief, including not more than $7,500 per TDPSA violation
sources.quality: law-firm commentary on the AG's first TDPSA enforcement action

statutes.name: Texas Data Broker Law - civil penalty
statutes.citation: Tex. Bus. & Com. Code ch. 509 (data broker registration)
statutes.scope: Failure of a data broker to register, or misrepresentation in an application
statutes.notes: Secondary-source figure ($10,000 per violation) quoted from the AG's first privacy enforcement pleading; confirm against the codified section text.

sources.quote: including not more than $7,500 per TDPSA violation, a $10,000 penalty for violation of the Texas Data Broker Law
sources.quality: law-firm commentary on the AG's pleading

statutes.name: Illinois BIPA - statutory damages
statutes.enforcer: Private plaintiffs (state court / supplemental federal claim)
statutes.scope: Violations of BIPA duties: written policy (s.15(a)), notice and written release (s.15(b)), retention schedule (s.15(a)), disclosure limits (s.15(d)), profiting from biometrics (s.15(c))

aggregation.citation: 740 ILCS 14/20 as amended by Public Act 103-0769 (SB 2979, 2024)
aggregation.description: A private entity that collects or discloses the same person's biometric identifier more than once in violation of the Act has committed a single violation for which the person is entitled to at most one recovery. Counts must therefore be distinct persons, not scans.

statutes.notes: Liquidated damages of $1,000 per negligent violation or $5,000 per intentional/reckless violation, plus fees; multiple statutory duties breached against the same person do not create multiple recoveries after the 2024 amendment.

sources.quote: A prevailing party may recover for each violation: (1) against a private entity that negligently violates a provision of this Act, liquidated damages of $1,000 or actual damages, whichever is greater; (2) against a private entity that intentionally or recklessly violates a provision of this Act, liquidated damages of $5,000

Provides that a private entity that more than once collects or discloses a person's biometric identifier or biometric information from the same person in violation of the Act has committed a single violation for which the aggrieved person is entitled to, at most, one recovery.

statutes.name: Colorado Privacy Act - civil penalty
statutes.citation: Colo. Rev. Stat. s. 6-1-1315; penalties via s. 6-1-112
statutes.scope: Violations of the Colorado Privacy Act, enforced as deceptive trade practices under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act
statutes.notes: No statutory aggregate cap since 2019. The $20,000 figure is the Colorado Consumer Protection Act maximum per violation; the CPA does not set its own number. Confirm the current cap before relying on it.

sources.quote: The CPA tasked the Colorado Attorney General with implementing and enforcing the CPA ... The CPA is a part of the State of Colorado's Consumer Protection Act
Violations are deceptive trade practices under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act, with civil penalties up to $20,000 per violation and no cap on aggregate penalties since 2019

statutes.name: Washington My Health My Data Act - penalties via the Consumer Protection Act
statutes.enforcer: Washington Attorney General and private plaintiffs
statutes.scope: Violations of the My Health My Data Act: consumer health data privacy policy, consent for collection/sharing, rights requests, security, geofencing restrictions, sale of health data
statutes.notes: RCW 19.373.090 makes a violation an unfair or deceptive act under the Consumer Protection Act (RCW 19.86); the Attorney General may seek up to $7,500 per violation under RCW 19.86.140, and consumers have a private right of action for actual damages, fees and injunctive relief.

sources.quote: Chapter 19.373 RCW - WASHINGTON MY HEALTH MY DATA ACT ... 19.373.090 Application of consumer protection act
sources.quality: primary legislation (Washington State Legislature section index)
